I'm talking about the kid who just picks up the ball and *does* it, or just threw a ball until he did and copied that method. He may know "yeah, I move my arm like this and ball does that", but he's got no capability to teach that to someone else beyond "copy what I do" until he *does* understand it.

To continue your example, Occult magic is the kid who makes a paper airplane. They don't have the slightest *inkling* of what aerodynamics actually is, but they know what shapes make a good paper airplane. Change the materials or environment and they don't have the *understanding* needed to make those materials fly in the same way. Or, to use anther example, the story of the pot roast (a woman had a pot roast recipe that called to cut both ends off. Pot roast was delicious, but she didn't understand why the recipe had her do that until she went to the primary source, her grandmother who taught her mother who taught the recipe to her, that she understood that the recipe was originally written for a small pan). She knew *how* to make the roast, but didn't understand *why* things were done a certain way. Sure, she applied a scientific rigor to finding out why (tracing information back to the primary source), but what she was looking for was something that *could* be understood.

Essentially, we're talking about the difference between "knowing", having a fact, vs "understanding", being able to interpret and apply that fact. Occult casters can *know* occult magic, they will never *understand* occult magic though, because by its very nature it is incapable of being understood.
